decisions.statement: A round is asked for here rather than run here.
The round asked for is asked of the audit service over HTTP and waited on.
The round asked for names the commit the caller needs judged.
A check's verdict is read from the audit log beside that check's page.
The page a check's slug names is read from the index.
A check the index names no page for has no verdict, so it goes unanswered.
A caller may hand over a reading of its own in place of that one.
A caller may hand over a round of its own in place of asking the service.
The reading of the verdicts beside the pages is reached by whoever runs a round.
A verdict at the commit asked or at a descendant of it answers for that commit.
A verdict that refused answers as much as a verdict that refused nothing.
A check every verdict already answers for is owed no round.
A check owed a round is named in the round asked for.
A check no round is owed for is named in none.
A round is asked for once.
A round is asked for only where a check is still unanswered.
The verdict a round answered is read from what came back rather than from a log.
A check unanswered after that is named rather than answered clean.
A round that would not start leaves every check it was owed unanswered.
A round that ran is named on a list the caller hands in, with the checks asked.
A caller wanting none of that naming hands in no list.
A refusal is named with the check that refused it.
A refusal is named with the commit its verdict is at.
A check that could not run is named apart from a check that refused.
Nothing here runs a check.
Nothing here writes a verdict.
Nothing here says which checks run at audit.

definition: a round of the audit service asked for at a commit, and what its verdicts say
